title: Integrating imaging and biopsy-derived molecular markers for the pre-surgical detection of indolent and aggressive early stage lung adenocarcinoma
text:
There is currently no clinically accepted way to predict a lung cancer's likely aggressiveness prior to
removing the tumor via surgery, resulting in imprecise treatment. We propose to characterize the
aggressiveness of early-stage lung adenocarcinoma (the most common lung cancer subtype) before
treatment, based on detailed and quantitative analysis of chest CT and molecular analysis of a small
biopsy of the tumor obtained before surgery. The ability to determine the aggressiveness of lung cancer
could facilitate treatment tailored to individual patients: improving lung cancer survival in patients with
the most aggressive tumors and decreasing complications from lung cancer treatment in patients with
the least aggressive tumors.

title: Enhancing Risk Stratification in Alcoholic Hepatitis: Integrating AI-Based Radiomics with Clinical Predictors
text:
Alcoholic hepatitis (AH) is a life-threatening form of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) with limited
treatment options and high mortality rates. Current risk stratification tools for AH, such as MELD scores, are
inadequate in predicting clinical outcomes. This study aims to develop a novel AI-based radiomics model that
incorporates imaging biomarkers from CT scans with clinical data to improve the accuracy of mortality
prediction in hospitalized AH patients. By enhancing early risk stratification, the model may optimize treatment
decisions, reduce mortality, and improve the allocation of critical healthcare resources.

title: Developing and validating zebrafish models of tic disorders
text:
Tics are partially involuntary movements that significantly burden individuals and families, yet current therapies
are unsatisfactory. To screen the functional meaning of genetic mutations associated with tic disorders (TDs),
we propose to generate and validate zebrafish models, which are perfectly suited for large genetic screening
given their low cost and ease of use. These studies will help us identify new targets for TD treatments with better
efficacy and safety profiles.

title: Mechanisms of Base Excision DNA Repair
text:
Genomic integrity is challenged by spontaneous DNA damage that results from
endogenous and exogenous sources. This proposal focuses on elucidating the molecular mechanisms by
which cells detect and repair the most common forms of DNA damage, especially single strand breaks and
damaged bases. This information is critical to understanding the impact of genetic deficiencies, exposure to
carcinogens, and to improving cancer therapy.

title: Elucidating the role of PATZ1 in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma
text:
Neuroblastoma is the most common extra-cranial solid tumor affecting children, and the overall 5-year survival
for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma, which is characterized by MYCN-amplification, remains at about 50%.
Current therapies are aggressive with lifelong consequences, prompting the urgent need for improved therapies
for treating neuroblastoma. This project aims to validate PATZ1 as a dependency in neuroblastoma, uncover the
role of PATZ1 in disease pathogenicity, and biochemically characterize the epigenetic and transcriptional
consequences of PATZ1 loss in neuroblastoma, which could lead to a new therapeutic approach for treating
neuroblastoma.

title: Predoctoral Training: Innovative Technologies for Natural Products and Integrative Medicine Research
text: The program will train predoctoral students in basic science research related to dietary supplements (plant-based natural products) and complementary and integrative medicine. Scientists with training in this area play a critical role in ensuring the safety and efficacy of dietary supplements that are widely used by the general public.

title: Combinatorial Perturbation with Multi-Omics Readout to Dissect Etiology of Alzheimer's Disease Using Stem Cell and In Vivo Models
text:
Alzheimer's disease is a devastating disorder that affects millions of older adults, causing
progressive memory loss, cognitive decline, and disability. Our project aims to develop
innovative tools to better understand the complex genetic factors that contribute to Alzheimer's
risk, particularly how they interact with each other and with the aging process. By shedding light
on these mechanisms using the stem cell and in vivo model, our work has the potential to guide
the development of new strategies for diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease,
ultimately helping to reduce the immense burden on individuals, families, and society.

title: Ligand Gated Ion Channels Across Time and Space
text:
Ligand gated ion channels are proteins that enable our cells to fine-tune their intracellular environments based
on chemical cues, and the dysregulation of these proteins is a major driver of human disease. The details of how
ligand gated ion channels function are critical to understand for therapeutic design, yet despite their importance,
the mechanisms of function are unclear. We are elucidating the molecular mechanisms of how ligand gated ion
channels function to understand how they regulate our cells in health and provide foundations for disease
treatment.

title: SouthEast GEnomic Medicine eConsult Service (SE-GEMS)
text:
Integrating genomic medicine into routine healthcare holds immense promise for improving patient outcomes
through more timely testing, diagnosis, and precision therapeutics. To catalyze the integration of genomic
medicine into routine clinical care, we will create, implement, expand, and evaluate a region-wide genomic
medicine eConsult service. This effort aims to reach beyond the 5 million patients receiving care at our
institutions, to over 12 million residents in Alabama and Tennessee, and surrounding regions to create a
scable and sustainable service scalable to over 1,000 GM- eConsult per year.

title: Toward Systems Biophotonics: Imaging Biology across High Dimensions and Scales
text:
The proposed research program is relevant to public health because it advances imaging science and technology
to transform biomedical research. The results will open up novel methodological pathways and illuminate both
fundamental and translational discoveries. The proposed research is relevant to the part of NIGMS’s mission
that it advances basic biomedical research by supporting the development of biomedical technologies to enable
studies that underlie health and disease.

title: Prevention of anal cancer in People Living with HIV (PLWH)
text:
Anal cancer is caused mainly by sexually transmitted human papillomaviruses and has been increasing in
incidence for many years—especially in adults living with HIV. In fact, people living with HIV have a 100x
increased risk for anal cancer compared with HIV-negative patients. The VA cares for the largest population of
patients living with HIV of any healthcare system in the United States, over 25,000 Veterans in 2019. One
opportunity for preventing this deadly cancer in high-risk individuals lies in the effective treatment of
precancerous lesions. The proposed research uses several novel preclinical models of anal cancer to examine
the efficacy of targeted, topical therapies.

title: Image-guided, robot-assisted reduction of joint dislocation in orthopaedic surgery
text:
Accurate reduction of joint dislocations is challenged by uncertainties in reckoning 3D anatomy from 2D imaging, extended
use of fluoroscopy, and high risk of complications that can lead to poor functional outcomes, osteoarthritis, and disability.
Proposed work develops an image-guided robotic approach to enable accurate repair of the ankle syndesmosis through
automatic 3D planning, precise robotic execution, and intraoperative image-based confirmation. The solution combines
modern robotics approaches with intraoperative imaging to satisfy the high technical demands of joint realignment, limit
radiation dose to patient and staff, and provide accurate treatment to ultimately improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Novel Computational Framework for Free-Breathing & Ungated Dynamic MRI
text:
The main focus of this research is to develop a novel computational imaging framework for free
breathing dynamic MRI. The proposed framework will enable a novel free-breathing protocol for
the comprehensive evaluation of the heart and lung. The protocol is expected to enable the early
detection and management of pulmonary hypertension is subjects with pulmonary disorders.

title: Project 3: Biomarkers
text: PROJECT 3 ABSTRACT Accurate assessment of the multisystem phenotypic implications of an abnormal number of sex chromosomes, or sex chromosome aneuploidy (SCA), is a current limitation that needs to be overcome to facilitate effective clinical trials with targeted interventions and appropriate biomarkers. NASCARR Research Project 3, “Establishing Severity Scores and Predictive Biomarkers in SCA” will address this limitation by defining the dominant axes of clinical variation (ACV’s) for individuals with SCA and genomic biomarkers associated with ACV severity. In Aim 1, define dominant ACVs across SCA clinical domains and develop person-level outcome severity scores, we will apply our novel research methods for ACV discovery to Project 1 data – ~1,000 multidisciplinary outcome variables from ~1,000 karyotypically diverse individuals with SCA. Aim 1 will use cutting edge network science and machine learning methods to resolve dominant ACVs in SCA; differentiate shared vs distinct ACVs across medical specialties and SCA karyotypes; and enable rapid and standardized person-level measurement of outcome severity in SCA - for individual ACVs as well as all ACVs combined (global ACV severity). Crucially, our approach overcomes the siloing of information from different medical disciplines and SCA karyotypes that has impeded ACV definition and measurement in SCA to date. For Aim 2, specify genomic biomarkers for ACV severity in SCA, we will test the hypothesis that ACV severity can be predicted by sex chromosome gene expression. RNAseq will measure sex chromosome gene expression in individuals with the lowest and highest severity scores from four of the most common SCA karyotypes (X, XXX, XXY, XYY). Successful completion of aim 2 will result in the development of tools for genomic outcome prediction, identification of molecular predictors of outcome severity that could be measured or manipulated in clinical trials, and collection of polymorphic blood mononuclear cells (PMBCs) for future generation of stem cells for tissue-specific analyses. This project will be made possible through intramural NIH collaboration with extramural investigators in the NASCARR consortium, with the resources made possible through the RDCRN infrastructure.

title: PDX Trial Center for Breast Cancer Therapy
text:
The scientific premise of this Center is that breast cancer patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models represent the
diversity of human breast tumors, and can be feasibly utilized to test new drugs and drug combinations to find
therapeutic approaches that match with molecular features of various tumor types. The goal of our PDX
Development and Trials Center (PDTC) is to obtain preclinical data that will facilitate prioritization of drugs to
be tested in clinical trials at the National Cancer Institute (NCI). Toward this goal, our PDTC focuses on testing
drugs that are already available through the NCI as NCI-IND agents with the Experimental Therapeutics Clinical
Trials Network (ETCTN).

title: Reversible transformation of Anaplasma phagocytophilum using Cre-Lox recombination
text:
Obligately intracellular tick-borne disease agents, those that can only replicate inside a vertebrate or tick host
cell, are a severe and growing threat to human and animal health world-wide. Studying gene function of bacterial
pathogens using mutational analysis in which genes are inactivated by insertion of an interruptive sequence such
as a transposon, is an important step towards designing treatments and preventive strategies such as vaccines,
but this approach has been very difficult to implement with obligately intracellular bacteria, including those
transmitted by ticks. We have pioneered large-scale mutagenesis of tick-borne Anaplasma phagocytophilum in
human cells, demonstrated that mutant Rickettsia parkeri are safe and effective vaccinogens, and we now
propose to expand on these previous achievements by generating a library of A. phagocytophilum mutants in
which the function of mutated genes can be easily restored to verify mutant and wild-type phenotypes, and to
test the effect of mutations on mouse infectivity and tick transmissibility.

title: Development of AI-Augmented quality assurance tools for radiation therapy
text:
Development of AI-Augmented quality assurance tools for radiation therapy
Project narrative
This project is aimed at developing practical deep learning solutions for accurate and reliable treatment
plan verification. If successful, the research will substantially improve the safety, quality and efficiency
of radiation oncology practice, and enable patients to truly benefit from modern radiation therapy.

title: Design, prediction, and prioritization of systematic perturbations of the human genome
text:
The culmination of the proposal will be a systematic and comprehensive approach for interpreting noncoding
variants to understand the underlying mechanisms that link genetics to gene expression and causes of human
disease. That outcome will transform human disease studies by allowing noncoding sequence variation to
inform genetic causes of disease, both in novel disease gene discovery studies and in the diagnostic
interpretation of individual patient genomes.

title: Longitudinal examination of individual, social, and structural syndemics in drug overdose risk among people living with HIV (PLWH)
text:
People living with HIV (PLWH) are at increased risk of fatal drug overdose, however, little is known about
overdose risk factors in the context of polydrug use and HIV across different levels of the socio-ecological
model. This research will examine trajectories of drug overdose incidents, polydrug use, naloxone availability,
and medication for opioid use disorder access among PLWH during the fourth wave of the overdose crisis
(2019-2025) and the influence of the following syndemic risk factors: individual-level (Hepatitis C co-infection,
depression), social-level (intimate partner violence, childhood trauma), and structural-level (housing instability,
recent incarceration). This research will address gaps in understanding drug overdose incidents among PLWH
during the fourth wave of the overdose crisis and develop a framework for identifying risk factors for drug
overdose, which will inform overdose prevention practices among this vulnerable population.
